title: Distance-Independent Universality of Clifford+T
authors: Jens Palsberg, Keli Huang, Abdullah Almanei
abstract: A well-known theorem states that the Clifford+T gate set is universal for quantum computing. The theorem combines approximation using a distance measure on unitary matrices with equality up to global phase. Previous proofs combine these two notions for specific distance measures, but do not identify the properties that govern how they work together. Which properties are sufficient to state and prove the theorem?   We answer this question by defining projective distance measures using four axioms. We prove that the universality theorem holds for every distance measure satisfying these axioms. Thus, our formulation of the theorem is independent of any particular choice of distance measure. We show that the Hilbert-Schmidt distance is already a projective distance measure. We also develop a general construction that transforms a large class of distance measures into projective distance measures and apply it to obtain projective versions of the operator-norm distance, the Frobenius distance, and the trace distance. Finally, we formalize the proof of the universality theorem in Lean.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous, distance-independent criterion for the universality of the Clifford+T gate set in quantum computing. By defining 'projective distance measures' based on four axioms, the authors prove that the gate set can approximate any unitary operation for any distance metric satisfying these properties. This provides a fundamental theoretical underpinning for quantum circuit synthesis.
main_problem: To determine the necessary and sufficient properties of a distance measure required to prove the distance-independent universality of the Clifford+T gate set for quantum computation.
main_result: The universality theorem holds for any distance measure satisfying the axioms of a 'projective distance measure,' formalizing the proof in Lean.
method: The authors define projective distance measures using four axioms and prove that the gate set $\{C(X), H, T\}$ is universal with respect to any such measure by decomposing the approximation into sequential steps.
model_or_system: The system is quantum computation, focusing on approximating any arbitrary unitary matrix $U \in U(2^n)$ using the Clifford+T gate set.
key_observables: Distance measures (Hilbert-Schmidt, Trace, Operator-norm, Frobenius) and the approximation error $\epsilon$.
important_parameters: The structure of the distance measure (e.g., satisfying Projective Invariance) and the gate set $\{C(X), H, T\}$.
main_assumptions: The necessary structure for universality is captured entirely by the definition of a projective distance measure.
paper_structure: The paper first defines projective distance measures via four axioms.
